video.agency.evidence: [影魔·codex] 第1张第1行至第2行第2格（0–2.25秒），我持续悬浮、双爪低垂；面对右侧逐渐逼近的目标，看不出提前截击的准备。到第2行第3–5格（2.5–3秒）才抬爪、横扫，此时目标已经贴到我身前，属于检查项要求排除的“在敌人到跟前才出手”。拼图也无法确认枝臂擦中肩甲时我是否有受击反应。；[树人·claude] I'm judging this as the treants. What works: the first treant does advance from the right into the dark purple disc between 1.0 and 2.0s, turning white and cracked. Treants are then shattered at about 3.0–3.5s, 4.75–5.25s and 6.75–7.25s, which matches the spec's three swipes and three kills. What fails or can't be confirmed: (1) In the 2.0–2.5s frames, which the spec puts at about 2.3s, the first treant stands in front of him with its branch arms spread or hanging. I can't see a clear swing at him, and no sparks fly off his shoulder armour at 2.75–3.0s. The treant 'swings and strikes' that the spec requires, and the 'swings and strikes' at about 4.5s and 6.8s, can't be made out in the 4.25–4.5s and 6.25–6.5s frames either. To me the treants look like they are being hit while standing there. (2) From 2.0 to 3.75s, the second and third treants in the background stay at roughly the same distance and size near the tower. That reads as 'standing still waiting' rather than the full charge at about four steps per second the spec asks for. (3) Through 1.0–2.0s the first treant moves only a short distance per frame, which doesn't look like a full-speed run. At 4 fps I can't confirm the run speed or a continuous advance.

video.gaze.evidence: [影魔·codex] 第1张第2行第3–6格（2.5–3.25秒）、第3行第2–5格（4.25–5秒）、第4行第2–5格（6.25–7秒），我的头部细节不足以确认每次都先盯住当前目标再挥爪，不能仅凭手臂朝右攻击判定视线合格。第4行第7格至第5行第7格（7.5–9.5秒）也看不出规格要求的“目光扫过尸体”；头部基本维持原姿态，是否向下看尸体拿不准，按要求判fail。；[树人·claude] In the 1.5–1.75s frames the first treant, already turned white by the disc, has its body and head turned close to straight toward the camera rather than toward him on the left. That suggests it may be looking at the camera. At 4.0–4.5s and 6.0–6.5s the heads of the second and third treants are tiny, and I can't tell whether they are looking left at him. In the 2.0–3.5s frames the two background treants are too far away to show which way their heads face. At this thumbnail resolution I can't confirm that every treant keeps its eyes on him the whole way, so I'm judging this a fail.

video.readability.evidence: [audience·claude] Watched cold, the sheet reads clearly. A lava giant made of glowing fire stands on the left with a purple circle under its feet. Several tree people walk toward it from the right. There are three rounds of the same move. Round 1: the fist gathers a ring of fire at 2.50s and throws a fiery punch at 2.75s. It hits the nearest tree person with a burst of sparks at 3.00s, and that tree person flies backward, breaks apart and falls at 3.25–3.50s. Round 2: fire gathers at 4.25–4.50s, the hit lands on the second tree person at 4.75–5.00s, and it falls at 5.25–5.50s. Round 3: fire gathers at 6.25–6.50s, the hit lands at 6.75–7.00s, and that tree person is knocked into pieces at 7.25s. From 8.00s to 10.75s no tree people are standing; their bodies lie on the ground and only the lava giant is still up. Who cast the move (the lava giant), what it was (a fire punch), who it hit (each tree person in turn) and the result (all of them down) are all visible on screen. Small reservation: the fire effect at the moment of the hit is fairly small and close to the giant's body (e.g. 3.00s, 4.75s), and the giant barely moves while the tree people walk into the punch. That is less flashy than it could be, but it does not make the action hard to follow.
